title.en: Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8 - Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou
title.raw: 卷九十三 晉書19: 列傳八 盧質 李專美 盧詹 崔梲 薛融 曹國珍 張仁愿 趙熙 李遐 尹玉羽 鄭雲叟 Volume 93 Book of Later Jin 19: Biographies 8 - Lu Zhi, Li Zhuanmei, Lu zhan, Cui Zhuo, Xue Rong, Cao Guozhen, Zhang Renyuan, Zhao Xi, Li Xia, Yin Yuyu, Zheng Yunsou

sentences.zh: 盧質，字子徵，河南人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Zizheng, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖偲，唐太原府祁縣尉，累贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Si was magistrate of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture under Tang, and was posthumously promoted through several ranks to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Si had served as magistrate of Qi County in the Taiyuan prefecture under the Tang and was posthumously ennobled all the way to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖衍，唐刑部侍郎、太子賓客，累贈太保。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Minister of Justice and Mentor to the Heir Apparent under Tang, and was posthumously promoted through several ranks to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had been Vice Minister of Justice and Mentor to the Heir Apparent under the Tang and was posthumously raised in rank to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 父望，唐尚書司勛郎中，累贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: His father Wang was a Director in the Department of Merit and Demerit under the Ministry of Personnel in Tang, and was posthumously promoted through several ranks to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang had served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel's Department of Merit and Demerit under the Tang and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 質幼聰慧，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhi was clever in youth and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhi was exceptionally bright and showed a gift for writing.

sentences.zh: 年十六，陜帥王重盈奏授芮城令，能以色養。

translations.literal: At age sixteen the Shaanxi military commissioner Wang Chongying memorialized the throne to appoint him magistrate of Ruicheng, and he was able to support his parents with cheerful devotion.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen the Shaanxi commissioner Wang Chongying had him appointed magistrate of Ruicheng, where he already cared for his parents with devoted warmth.

sentences.zh: 又為同州澄城令，從私便也。

translations.literal: He later served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, following his own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He later became magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, a post that suited his personal wishes.

sentences.zh: 秩滿改秘書郎，丁母憂，歸河南故裏。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was transferred to Secretary of the Palace Library; upon his mother's death he returned to his old home in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was made a secretary in the Palace Library, and after his mother died he went home to Henan.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，北遊太原，時李襲吉在武皇幕府，以女妻之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he traveled north to Taiyuan; at that time Li Xiji was in the Military Governor's staff of the Martial Emperor, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianyou he went north to Taiyuan, where Li Xiji served on the staff of Li Keyong and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武皇憐其才，承制授檢校兵部郎中，充河東節度掌書記，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor took pity on his talent and, by imperial order on his own authority, appointed him Acting Director in the Ministry of War, to serve as secretary on the staff of the Hedong military commission, and granted him the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong admired his ability and, acting on his own authority, named him acting director in the Ministry of War and secretary to the Hedong command, also granting him the crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 武皇厭代，其弟克寧握兵柄，有嗣襲之望，質與張承業等密謀，同立莊宗為嗣，有翊贊之功。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor died, his younger brother Kening held military power and had hopes of succeeding to the succession; Zhi secretly plotted with Zhang Chengye and others, and together they established Zhuangzong as heir, for which he had the merit of assisting and supporting.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Keyong's death his brother Kening controlled the army and hoped to take the succession, but Zhi conspired in secret with Zhang Chengye and others to install Zhuangzong as heir—a service for which he later received credit.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗四征，質皆從行。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong undertook his four campaigns, Zhi accompanied him on every one.
translations.idiomatic: On all four of Zhuangzong's major campaigns Zhi marched at his side.

sentences.zh: 十六年，轉節度判官、檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to military commission judge and Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became judge on the military commission and acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莊宗將即帝位，命為大禮使，累加至銀青光祿大夫、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong was about to ascend the throne, he was appointed Commissioner of Grand Rites, and through successive promotions rose to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, on the eve of Zhuangzong's accession, he was made Commissioner of Grand Rites and was eventually promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授行臺禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was named Minister of Rites on the mobile secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既登極，欲相之，質性疏逸，不喜居高位，固辭獲免。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had taken the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi's nature was free and easy; he did not like holding high office and firmly declined, thereby escaping the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong was emperor he wanted Zhi as chief minister, but Zhi's easy temperament disliked high rank and he declined firmly until the offer was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼太原尹，充北京留守事，未赴任，改戶部尚書、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter, while retaining his original office, he was also made Prefect of Taiyuan and charged with the duties of northern capital regent, but before he took up the post he was changed to Minister of Revenue, Controller of Imperial Drafts, and Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was named Taiyuan prefect and northern capital regent while keeping his old title, but before he reported he was shifted to Minister of Revenue, controller of imperial drafts, and Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 同光元年冬，從平大梁，權判租庸事，逾月隨駕都洛，旋受詔權知汴州軍府事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the pacification of Daliang, was temporarily put in charge of tax and corvée affairs, and a month later accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang; he then received an edict to act as administrator of the Bianzhou military government.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tongguang 1 he took part in the conquest of Daliang, temporarily oversaw tax and corvée matters, followed the court to Luoyang a month later, and was soon ordered to administer Bianzhou's military government.

sentences.zh: 時孔謙握利權，志在聚斂，累移文於汴，配民放絲，質堅論之，事雖不行，時論賞之。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Qian held financial power and aimed at amassing revenue; he repeatedly sent documents to Bian ordering the people levied to deliver silk, and Zhi argued against it firmly; though the matter was not carried out, public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian then controlled finance and was bent on squeezing revenue, repeatedly ordering Bian to levy silk from the populace; Zhi protested vigorously, and although his advice was ignored, contemporaries applauded him.

sentences.zh: 俄又改金紫光祿大夫、兵部尚書、知制誥、翰林學士承旨，仍賜論思匡佐功臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was again changed to Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, Controller of Imperial Drafts, and Hanlin Academician-in-Chief, and was also granted the merit title "Counsel in Reflection and Aid in Governance."
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, controller of drafts, and Hanlin chief, and received the merit title Counsel in Reflection and Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 會覆試進士，質以「後從諫則聖」為賦題，以「堯、舜、禹、湯傾心求過」為韻，舊例賦韻四平四側，質所出韻乃五平三側，由是大為識者所誚。

translations.literal: When he presided over the re-examination of presented scholars, Zhi set the fu topic "If one later follows remonstrance, one becomes sage" and used the rhyme phrase "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang bent their hearts to seek their faults"; the old rule for fu rhymes was four level tones and four oblique tones, but the rhymes Zhi produced were five level and three oblique, whereupon he was greatly ridiculed by the knowledgeable.
translations.idiomatic: During a re-examination of new jinshi candidates he set the fu topic "He who later heeds remonstrance becomes a sage" with the rhyme line on Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang seeking their faults; custom required four level and four oblique rhymes, but Zhi gave five level and three oblique, and learned opinion mocked him roundly.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，制授特進、檢校司空、同州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, by imperial order he was appointed Special Advancement, Acting Minister of Works, and military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 1 he was formally made Special Advancement, acting Minister of Works, and commissioner of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時宰相馮道以詩餞別，其警句云：「視草北來唐學士，擁旄西去漢將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Feng Dao wrote a farewell poem; its striking lines read: "A Tang academician who viewed the drafts came from the north; a Han general who grasped the bannered staff goes west."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Feng Dao wrote a parting poem whose memorable lines ran: "From the north, a Tang scholar who reviewed the drafts; to the west, a Han general who takes up the commander's staff."

sentences.zh: 」儒者榮之。

translations.literal: " Confucian scholars counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters took the compliment as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，改賜耀忠匡定保節功臣，就加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted instead the merit title "Merit in Glorifying Loyalty, Rectifying and Securing, and Preserving Integrity," and at the same time was further promoted to Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the merit title Glorifying Loyalty, Rectifying and Securing, and Preserving Integrity and was promoted on the spot to acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 三年，入拜兵部尚書，判太僕卿事。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court to receive appointment as Minister of War and was assigned to adjudicate the affairs of the Minister of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to court as Minister of War and was also put in charge of the Imperial Studs.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封開國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke Who Founds the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Founds the State.

sentences.zh: 長興二年，授檢校太保、河陽節度使，未幾，移鎮滄州，入為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed Acting Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Heyang; before long he was transferred to command Cang Prefecture, then entered court as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 2 he became acting Grand Mentor and commissioner of Heyang, soon moved to Cangzhou, and then returned to court as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及秦王得罪，奉詔權知河南府事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin fell into disgrace, he received an edict to act as administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Qin was condemned he was ordered to administer Henan Prefecture on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 應順初，遷檢校太傅，正拜河南尹，後改太子少師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was transferred to Acting Grand Preceptor, formally appointed Prefect of Henan, and later changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yingshun he was made acting Grand Preceptor and full prefect of Henan, and later became Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，復為右僕射。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai he again served as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，質以微恙分司洛宅。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhi, on account of a slight illness, took a nominal post and resided at his Luoyang mansion.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne Zhi retired to a nominal post at his Luoyang home because of a minor ailment.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，拜太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor came to the throne Zhi was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於洛陽，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang, at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Luoyang in the autumn of Tianfu 7, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 累贈太子太師，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: Through successive posthumous promotions he was raised to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the temple name Wenzhong (Cultured and Loyal).

translations.literal: [Annotation:]
translations.idiomatic: [Annotation:]

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：漢乾祐元年九月，其子尚書兵部員外郎盧瓊上章請謚，下太常議，謚曰文忠。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Five Dynasties Assembly of Essentials: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianyou under Han, his son Lu Qiong, Outer Director in the Ministry of War under the Secretariat, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Assembly of Essentials for the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of Han Qianyou 1 his son Lu Qiong, an outer director in the Ministry of War, petitioned for a posthumous title; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and approved Wenzhong.)〉

sentences.zh: 子十一人，唯第六子夏，仕至省郎，余歷州縣焉。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; only the sixth, Xia, rose in office to a director in the central ministries, while the rest served through prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Of his eleven sons only the sixth, Xia, reached a post in the central ministries; the others served in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 李專美，字翊商，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhuanmei, courtesy name Yishang, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhuanmei, courtesy name Yishang, came from Wannian in the Jingzhao metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 曾祖隨，光祿卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sui was Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sui had been Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 祖正範，尚書庫部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhengfan was a Director in the Department of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhengfan had served as director in the Ministry of Works' Department of Storehouses.

sentences.zh: 專美少篤學文，以父樞唐昭宗時常應進士舉，為覆試所落，不許再入，專美心愧之，由是不遊文場。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei in youth devoted himself to learning and literature; because his father Shu in the time of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang had repeatedly entered the jinshi examination and was failed in the re-examination, and was not permitted to enter again, Zhuanmei felt ashamed in his heart and therefore did not enter the literary arena.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei studied literature diligently as a youth, but his father Shu had failed the jinshi re-examination under Emperor Zhaozong and was barred from trying again—a humiliation Zhuanmei felt keenly, so he never entered the examination halls himself.

sentences.zh: 偽梁貞明中，河南尹張全義以專美名族之後，奏為陸渾尉，秩滿，改舞陽令。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era of the false Liang, Zhang Quanyi, Prefect of Henan, because Zhuanmei was descended from a famous clan, memorialized the throne to appoint him Assistant Magistrate of Luhun; when his term ended he was changed to magistrate of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Liang's Zhenming era Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi, noting his eminent lineage, had him appointed assistant magistrate of Luhun and later magistrate of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 專美性廉謹，大著政聲。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei's nature was incorrupt and cautious, and he won great renown in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and careful by nature, he earned a strong reputation as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成中，安邑榷鹽使李肅辟為推官，時唐末帝鎮河中，見其敦雅，心重之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, Commissioner of the Anyi Salt Monopoly, recruited him as investigating officer; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was military governor of Hezhong, saw his solid elegance, and valued him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Tang's Tiancheng era Li Su of the Anyi salt monopoly took him on as investigating officer while the future Last Emperor of Tang, then governing Hezhong, was impressed by his sober refinement and came to esteem him.

sentences.zh: 末帝一日曾召肅宴於衙署，專美亦預坐，末帝謂肅曰：「某夜來夢主上召去，與宋王同剃卻頭，何也？

translations.literal: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet in the government office, and Zhuanmei also took a seat; the Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me away and shaved my head together with the Prince of Song—what does it mean?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the prince summoned Su to dine at headquarters with Zhuanmei present and said to Su: "Last night I dreamed the emperor called me in and shaved my head along with the Prince of Song—what do you make of that?"

sentences.zh: 」坐客都無對者，專美屏人謂曰：「將來必為嗣主。

translations.literal: " None of those seated had any reply; Zhuanmei, sending others aside, said to him: "In the future you will surely become the heir and sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: " No one at the table could answer; Zhuanmei drew him aside and said quietly: "You are destined to become heir and emperor."

sentences.zh: 」由是愈重焉。

translations.literal: " From this he valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment the prince valued him even more highly.

sentences.zh: 末帝留守長安，奏為從事，及移鎮鳳翔，遷為記室。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was regent at Chang'an, he memorialized to appoint Zhuanmei as staff officer; when he was transferred to govern Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.
translations.idiomatic: While the prince held Chang'an as regent he had Zhuanmei appointed to his staff, and when he moved to Fengxiang he made him recorder.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，除尚書庫部郎中，賜金紫，充樞密院直學士。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zhuanmei was appointed Director in the Department of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works, granted the gold-purple insignia, and made a direct academician of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: On the Last Emperor's accession he became director in the Ministry of Works' Department of Storehouses, received the gold-purple insignia, and served as a direct academician of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 初，末帝起自鳳翔，大許諸軍厚賞。

translations.literal: At first, when the Last Emperor rose from Fengxiang, he made great promises of lavish rewards to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When he first rose from Fengxiang the Last Emperor had promised the armies lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 洎至洛陽，閱內庫金帛不過二三萬，尋又配率京城戶民，雖行捶楚，亦所獲無幾，末帝憂之。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Luoyang, examination of the inner treasury's gold and silks showed no more than twenty or thirty thousand; soon they also levied assessments on the households of the capital, and though they applied beating and torture, what was obtained was still very little, and the Last Emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Luoyang he found scarcely twenty or thirty thousand strings in the inner treasury, then tried levies on the capital's households—even with beatings the yield was tiny, and the emperor grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 會專美宿於禁中，末帝召而讓之曰：「卿士人子弟，常言有才術，今致我至此，不能度運以濟時事，留才術何施也！

translations.literal: Once when Zhuanmei was lodging in the forbidden precincts, the Last Emperor summoned and reproached him, saying: "You are the son of a scholar-official family and always speak of talent and ability; yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot gauge the times to rescue current affairs—of what use is talent left unused!"
translations.idiomatic: One night while Zhuanmei was staying in the palace the emperor summoned him and upbraided him: "You are a scholar's son who boasts of talent—yet you have landed me in this fix and cannot read the times to save the realm. What good is unused ability?"

sentences.zh: 」專美惶恐待罪，良久奏曰：「臣才力駑劣，屬當興運，陛下猥垂錄任，無以裨益聖朝，然府藏空竭，軍賞不給，非臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Zhuanmei in fear and trembling awaited punishment; after a long while he memorialized, saying: "Your servant's talent and strength are dull and inferior; I happened to meet a time of rising fortune, and Your Majesty was kind enough to record and employ me, yet I have been unable to benefit the sagely court—still, the government storehouses are empty and exhausted and army rewards cannot be supplied; this is not your servant's crime."
translations.idiomatic: " Trembling, Zhuanmei waited to be punished, then after a long pause replied: "My abilities are meager, and though Your Majesty honored me with office I have done little for the court—but empty treasuries and unpaid soldiers are not my fault alone."

sentences.zh: 臣思明宗棄代之際，是時府庫濫賞已竭，繼以鄂王臨朝，紀綱大壞，縱有無限之財賦，不能滿驕軍溪壑之心，所以陛下孤立岐陽而得天下。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that at the time when Emperor Mingzong abandoned the throne, the treasury had already been drained by reckless rewards; this was followed by the Prince of E holding court, when statutes and discipline were greatly ruined—even if there had been limitless wealth and revenue, it could not fill the insatiable hearts of the arrogant armies like ravines and gullies, and therefore Your Majesty, isolated at Qiyang, was able to gain the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Mingzong's abdication: the treasury was already emptied by reckless largesse, then the Prince of E ruled and discipline collapsed—no amount of wealth could satisfy armies grown insatiable, which is why Your Majesty, alone at Qiyang, could seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣以為國之存亡，不專在行賞，須刑政立於上，恥格行於下，賞當功，罰當罪，則近於理道也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that a state's survival or destruction does not depend solely on dispensing rewards; punishments and government must be established above, and the norm of shame must be practiced below—rewards fitting merit, punishments fitting crime—then one approaches the way of principle.
translations.idiomatic: A state's survival, I believe, does not rest on rewards alone: law must stand firm above, shame must guide conduct below, rewards must match merit and punishments match guilt—only then does government approach right principle.

sentences.zh: 若陛下不改覆車之轍，以賞無賴之軍，徒困蒸民，存亡未可知也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not change the track of the overturned cart and uses rewards for unruly armies, you will only weary the common people, and whether the state survives or perishes cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not turn from the path that wrecked your predecessors and keeps bribing unruly troops, you will only crush the people—and the realm's fate will be anyone's guess.

sentences.zh: 今宜取見在財賦以給之，不必踐前言而希茍悅。

translations.literal: Now you should take the wealth and revenue presently on hand to supply them, and need not fulfill earlier words in hope of shallow favor.
translations.idiomatic: Pay them from what wealth you actually have; do not strain to keep old promises merely to win a cheap popularity.

sentences.zh: 」末帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及其行賞，雖不愜於軍士，然洛陽戶民獲免鞭笞之苦，由專美之敷揚也。

translations.literal: When rewards were distributed, although the soldiers were not satisfied, yet the households of Luoyang were spared the suffering of the whip and staff—this was due to Zhuanmei's exposition and advocacy.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were paid out the troops were displeased, but Luoyang households were spared the lash—thanks to Zhuanmei's counsel.

sentences.zh: 尋轉給事中，明年，遷兵部侍郎、端明殿學士，未幾，改檢校尚書右僕射、守秘書監，充宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Duanming Hall; before long he was changed to Acting Right Vice Director under the Secretariat, acting Director of the Palace Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became supervising censor, the next year vice minister of war and Duanming academician, then acting Right Vice Director, acting palace librarian, and commissioner of the northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，以例除名。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was removed from office according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took Luoyang he was dismissed under the usual purge of the previous regime's officials.

sentences.zh: 三年，復授衛尉少卿，繼遷鴻臚、大理卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Guard, and subsequently promoted to Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was restored as vice minister of the imperial guard, then promoted to minister of ceremonies and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 開運中，以病卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness during the Kaiyun era, aged sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 專美之遠祖本出姑臧大房，與清河小房崔氏、北祖第二房盧氏、昭國鄭氏為四望族，皆不以才行相尚，不以軒冕為貴，雖布衣徒步，視公卿蔑如也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors originally came from the great branch at Guzang, and together with the minor branch of the Cui at Qinghe, the second branch of the northern ancestor of the Lu, and the Zheng of Zhaoguo formed the four eminent clans; none prized one another for conduct and talent, none held carriage and cap as noble—even in plain cloth and on foot they looked down on public ministers as though they were nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei's forebears belonged to the great Guzang line, one of the four great clans alongside the Qinghe Cui, the northern Lu, and the Zhaoguo Zheng—clans that cared nothing for merit, disdained high office, and treated even grand ministers with contempt while dressed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 男女婚嫁，不雜他姓，欲聘其族，厚贈金帛始許焉。

translations.literal: In marriage for men and women they did not mix with other surnames; those who wished to betroth into their clans had first to present thick gifts of gold and silks before consent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They married only within the clan; suitors from outside had to offer lavish gifts of gold and silk before a match was even considered.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗曾降詔以戒其弊風，終莫能改。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict to warn against this corrupt custom, yet in the end it could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Taizong of Tang issued an edict condemning the practice, yet it never changed.

sentences.zh: 其間有未達者，必曰：「姓崔、盧、李、鄭了，余復何求耶！

translations.literal: Among them those who had not risen in office would invariably say: "One's surname is Cui, Lu, Li, or Zheng—what more does one seek!"
translations.idiomatic: Those among them who had not risen in office would say: "With a surname of Cui, Lu, Li, or Zheng, what more could one want?"

sentences.zh: 」其遠者，則邈在天表，敻若千里，人罕造其門，浮薄自大，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " The more remote among them were as distant as the sky above, remote as a thousand li; people rarely came to their gates—frivolous, shallow, and arrogant, all were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: The loftiest branches seemed to live beyond the clouds, a thousand li away; few visitors crossed their thresholds—all alike in shallow arrogance.

sentences.zh: 唯專美未嘗以氏族形於口吻，見寒素士大夫，恒恂恂如也，人以此多之。

translations.literal: Only Zhuanmei never let his clan appear on his lips; when he met poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and for this people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanmei alone never flaunted his lineage; toward humble scholars he was always courteous, and people admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 專美職岐下，曾夢具裳簡立嵩山之頂。

translations.literal: While Zhuanmei held office below Qi, he once dreamed that he stood on the summit of Mount Song fully robed and holding the memorial tablet.
translations.idiomatic: While serving under the prince at Qiyang he dreamed he stood on Mount Song's peak in full court dress holding the memorial tablet.

sentences.zh: 及為端明殿學士，學士李崧同列而班在其上，因以所夢告崧，且言：「某非德非勛，安可久居此位，處吾子之首乎！

translations.literal: When he became an academician of the Duanming Hall, the academician Li Song was in the same row yet ranked above him; he therefore told Song of his dream and said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this post and stand above you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: As a Duanming academician he sat in the same row as Li Song, who ranked above him; he told Song of the dream and said: "I have neither virtue nor merit—how can I keep a post that places me above you?"

sentences.zh: 」因懇求他官，尋移宣徽使，崧深德之。

translations.literal: " He therefore earnestly requested another office and soon was transferred to commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; Song was deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He begged for another post and soon moved to the Palace Secretariat commissionership; Song felt deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及高祖臨朝，崧為樞密使，與桑維翰同列，維翰與專美亦有舊，乃協力以奏之，遂復朝序，位至九卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu presided at court, Song was Privy Council commissioner and sat in the same row as Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and they joined forces to memorialize on his behalf, whereupon he was restored to court rank and rose to one of the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Song was privy council commissioner alongside Sang Weihan, who also knew Zhuanmei well; together they secured his restoration to court rank until he reached one of the nine ministries.

sentences.zh: 專美曾使閩中，遇風水漂至兩浙，逾歲無恙而還，至是善終，人以為神道福謙之所致也。

translations.literal: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min; he encountered wind and waves and was driven adrift to the two Zhe regions, and after more than a year returned unharmed; when he now ended his life well, people took it as brought about by the spirits' blessing of humility.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Min he was blown by storm to the lower Yangtze and returned unharmed after more than a year; when he died peacefully at last, people attributed it to divine favor for his modesty.

sentences.zh: 崔棁，字子文，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhuo, courtesy name Ziwen, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhuo, courtesy name Ziwen, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 累世冠冕。

translations.literal: For generations his family had worn court caps and held office.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held office for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元受，舉進士，直史館。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuanshou passed the jinshi examination and served on duty at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuanshou was a jinshi graduate who served in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 祖銖，安、濮二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhu was prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhu had been prefect of An and Pu.

sentences.zh: 父涿，刑部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Zhuo was a Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuo had been a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 棁少好學，梁貞明三年，舉進士甲科，為開封尹王瓚從事。

translations.literal: Zhuo in youth loved learning; in the third year of Zhenming under Liang he passed the jinshi in the first class and became a staff officer to Wang Zan, Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo studied diligently as a youth; in Liang Zhenming 3 he graduated jinshi in the top class and joined the staff of Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan.

sentences.zh: 棁性至孝，父涿有疾，謂親友曰：「死生有命，無醫為也。

translations.literal: Zhuo's nature was supremely filial; when his father Zhuo fell ill he said to relatives and friends: "Life and death have their allotted span—there is no use in physicians."
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, when his father fell ill Zhuo told friends and kin: "Life and death are fated—physicians are useless."

sentences.zh: 」棁侍之衣不解帶，有賓至，必拜泣告於門外，請方便勸其進藥，涿終莫之從。

translations.literal: " Zhuo attended him without undoing his belt for days on end; when guests arrived he would bow and weep, reporting outside the gate and asking them tactfully to urge his father to take medicine, yet Zhuo in the end never complied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo nursed him without loosening his belt for days; when visitors came he bowed and wept at the gate, begging them to persuade his father to take medicine, but Zhuo never yielded.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，哀毀過制。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his father, his grief and devastation exceeded the prescribed norms.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father his grief exceeded every prescribed limit.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，授監察御史，不應命，逾年詔再下，乃就列焉。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Mingzong he was appointed Investigating Censor but did not accept the commission; after more than a year the edict was issued again, and only then did he take his place in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong he was named investigating censor but declined; more than a year later a second edict brought him to accept the post.

sentences.zh: 累遷都官郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Director in the Department of Justice under the Ministry of Justice and a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Justice's Department of Punishments and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 天福初，以戶部侍郎為學士承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu he became vice minister of revenue and Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗草制，為宰相桑維翰所改，棁以唐故事，學士草制有所改者，當罷職，乃引經據爭，維翰不能詰，命權知二年貢舉。

translations.literal: Once when he drafted an edict it was altered by the chief minister Sang Weihan; Zhuo cited Tang precedent that when an academician's draft edict was changed he should be dismissed from office, and citing classics he disputed the matter; Weihan could not rebut him and ordered him to act as administrator of the second year's civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When chief minister Sang Weihan altered one of his drafts, Zhuo cited Tang precedent that an academician whose edict was rewritten must leave office and argued from the classics until Weihan could not answer; he was then put in charge of the second year's examinations.

sentences.zh: 時有進士孔英者，素有醜行，為當時所惡，棁受命往見維翰，維翰語素簡，謂棁曰：「孔英來矣。

translations.literal: At that time there was a presented scholar named Kong Ying who had long had disgraceful conduct and was detested by contemporaries; Zhuo received orders to go see Weihan, and Weihan's words were always brief; he said to Zhuo: "Kong Ying has come."
translations.idiomatic: A candidate named Kong Ying was notorious for scandalous behavior and widely despised; when Zhuo went to see Weihan on examination business the terse minister said only: "Kong Ying has come."

sentences.zh: 」棁不諭其意，以謂維翰以孔英為言，乃考英及第，物議大以為非，遂罷學士，拜尚書左丞，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: " Zhuo did not grasp his meaning and supposed that Weihan was speaking of Kong Ying, and therefore examined Ying as having passed; public opinion greatly condemned this as wrong, and he was thereupon dismissed as academician, appointed Left Assistant Director under the Secretariat, and promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Misunderstanding the remark as approval, Zhuo passed Kong Ying—a decision public opinion fiercely condemned. He was removed as Hanlin academician, made Left Assistant Director under the Secretariat, and then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後以風痹改太子賓客，分司西京。

translations.literal: Later, on account of wind paralysis, he was changed to Mentor to the Heir Apparent with a nominal post in the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted with rheumatism, he became Mentor to the Heir Apparent with a nominal post in the western capital.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 棁平生所著文章、碑誄、制詔甚多，人有借本傳寫者，則曰：「有前賢，有來者，奚用此為！

translations.literal: Zhuo in his lifetime composed a great many essays, epitaphs, eulogies, and edicts; when people asked to borrow his drafts to copy them he would say: "There are former worthies and there are those yet to come—of what use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a great many essays, epitaphs, and edicts in his lifetime; when anyone asked to copy his drafts he would say: "Past masters and future writers exist—why bother with mine?"

sentences.zh: 」凡受托而作者，必親劄致之，即焚其槁，懼泄人之假手也。

translations.literal: " Whenever he composed on commission he would personally deliver the letter and then burn the draft, fearing that others might leak his work through borrowed hands.
translations.idiomatic: For commissioned pieces he always delivered them in person and burned the draft, lest someone pass off his writing as their own.

sentences.zh: 棁笑不至矧，怒不至詈，接新進後生，未嘗無誨焉。

translations.literal: When Zhuo laughed it did not reach a grin; when angry he did not reach cursing; in receiving newly advanced younger men he never lacked instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His smile never broadened into a grin, his anger never broke into abuse, and he always offered guidance to younger men newly entering office.

sentences.zh: 群居公會端坐寡言，嘗雲非止致人愛憎，且或幹人祖禰之諱。

translations.literal: In gatherings at public assemblies he sat upright and spoke little, once saying that this was not only to avoid causing others' love or hatred, but also lest one touch the taboo names of others' ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At public gatherings he sat quietly and spoke little, remarking that silence not only avoided stirring likes and dislikes but also kept one from violating ancestral name taboos.

sentences.zh: 指命仆役，亦用禮節，盛暑祁寒，不使冒犯。

translations.literal: In directing and commanding servants he also used ritual propriety; in extreme summer heat or severe winter cold he did not let them suffer offense.
translations.idiomatic: Even in giving orders to servants he observed propriety and would not let them be abused in blazing heat or bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 嘗自話於知友云：「某少時，夢二人前引行路，一人計地裏，曰：『一舍矣，可以止。

translations.literal: He once told close friends: "In my youth I dreamed that two men led me forward on the road; one reckoned the distance in li and said: 'One stage already—we may stop.'"
translations.idiomatic: He once told friends: "As a youth I dreamed two men led me along a road; one counted the li and said, 'One stage—you may stop here.'"

sentences.zh: 』一人曰：『此君當更進三十有八里。

translations.literal: ' The other said: 'This gentleman should go thirty-eight li farther.'"
translations.idiomatic: The other said, 'This man must go another thirty-eight li.'"

sentences.zh: 』復行如所言，二人皆止之，俄而驚覺。

translations.literal: ' They went on again as spoken, and both men stopped him; presently he woke with a start.
translations.idiomatic: They walked on as told until both men halted him, and then he woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 」棁常識是夢，以為定命之限，故六十七請退，明年果終焉。

translations.literal: " Zhuo always recognized this dream and took it as the limit of allotted fate; therefore at sixty-seven he requested retirement, and the next year he indeed ended his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo took the dream as a sign of his allotted span, retired at sixty-seven, and died the following year as foretold.

sentences.zh: 兄棆，有隱德，好釋氏，閑居滑州。

translations.literal: His elder brother Lun had hidden virtue, loved Buddhism, and lived in retirement at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Lun, a man of quiet virtue who favored Buddhism, lived in retirement in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲訪人於白馬津北，及臨岸，嘆曰：「波勢洶湧如此，安可濟乎！

translations.literal: Once he wished to visit someone north of the Baima Ford; when he came to the bank he sighed and said: "The waves are surging so fiercely—how can one cross!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, intending to visit someone north of the Baima Ford, he reached the bank and sighed: "The current runs so wild—how could anyone cross?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So he turned back.

sentences.zh: 後征拜左拾遺，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder, but he declined on grounds of illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later summoned as Left Reminder, he pleaded illness and never took office.

sentences.zh: 薛融，汾州平遙人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong was a native of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong came from Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性純和，以儒學為業。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and gentle, and he took Confucian learning as his profession.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and upright by nature, he devoted himself to Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 初從雲州帥李存璋為幕職，唐莊宗平河南，歷鄆、徐二鎮從事。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yun Prefecture commander Li Cunzhang as a staff officer; when Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he served successively as staff officer in the Yan and Xu commands.
translations.idiomatic: He first served on the staff of Yun commander Li Cunzhang; after Zhuangzong pacified Henan he held staff posts in the Yan and Xu commands.

sentences.zh: 明宗初，授華州節度判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mingzong's reign he was appointed judge of the Hua military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingzong's reign he became judge on the Hua military commission.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，入為右補闕，直宏文館，歲餘，改河東觀察判官，會高祖鎮太原，遂居於幕府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Reminder and served on duty at the Hongwen Institute; after more than a year he was changed to judge of the Hedong observation commission; as it happened Gaozu was governing Taiyuan, and he thereupon resided in the military governor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 4 he entered court as Right Reminder with duty at the Hongwen Institute; a year later he became judge on the Hedong observation commission and joined Gaozu's staff when the future emperor governed Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，高祖將舉義，延賓席而歷問之，次及融，對曰：「融本儒生，只曾讀三五卷書，至於軍旅之事，進退存亡之機，未之學也。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, as Gaozu was about to raise the righteous standard, he extended a banquet for guests and questioned them in turn; when it came to Rong, he replied: "Rong is originally a Confucian scholar and has only read three or five volumes of books; as for military affairs and the timing of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have not studied them."
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai, as Gaozu prepared to rebel, he questioned his guests in turn at a banquet; when Rong's turn came he said: "I am only a scholar who has read a handful of books—I know nothing of armies or the calculus of survival."

sentences.zh: 」座中聳然。

translations.literal: " Those seated were startled upright.
translations.idiomatic: The guests sat up in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 及登極，遷尚書吏部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Rong was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel under the Secretariat, concurrently Serving Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Rong became director in the Ministry of Personnel and serving censor in charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，自左諫議大夫遷中書舍人，自以文學非優，不敢拜命，復為諫議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Counselor to Secretariat Drafter; considering his literary learning not superior, he did not dare accept the commission and returned to remonstrance counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 2 he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Counselor to Secretariat Drafter but, judging his literary talent inadequate, declined and resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 時詔修西京大內，融以鄴下用兵，國用不足，上疏復罷之，

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered repairs to the western capital's inner palace; Rong, because troops were engaged at Ye and state revenue was insufficient, submitted a memorial to have the project halted again,
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered repairs to the western capital palace, Rong memorialized to halt the work, citing the war at Ye and empty treasuries,

translations.literal: [Annotation:]
translations.idiomatic: [Annotation:]

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：薛融諫曰：「今宮室雖經焚毀，猶侈於帝堯之茅茨；

translations.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying: "Though the palaces have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched hut;"
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Xue Rong remonstrated: "Though the palaces have burned, they would still exceed Emperor Yao's thatched hut;")

sentences.zh: 所費雖寡，猶多於漢文之露臺。

translations.literal: the expense, though small, is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.
translations.idiomatic: and though the cost seems slight, it would still exceed Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.

sentences.zh: 況魏城未下，公私困窘，誠非陛下修宮館之日。

translations.literal: Moreover Weicheng has not yet fallen and public and private affairs are in distress—this is truly not the day for Your Majesty to repair palaces and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: With Weicheng still unconquered and state and people in distress, this is no time to rebuild palaces.

sentences.zh: 俟海內平寧，修之未晚。）〉

translations.literal: Wait until the realm within the seas is peaceful and settled—then repair will not be too late.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the empire is at peace—it will not be too late to rebuild.")〉

sentences.zh: 優詔嘉許。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 俄轉御史中丞，秩滿改尚書右丞，分司西都。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; when his term ended he was changed to Right Assistant Director under the Secretariat with a nominal post in the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became censor-in-chief, then after his term ended was made Right Assistant Director with a nominal post in the western capital.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，以疾卒，年六十餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness, at age sixty-some.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in Tianfu 6, in his sixties.

sentences.zh: 曹國珍，字彥輔，幽州固安人也。

translations.literal: Cao Guozhen, courtesy name Yanfu, was a native of Gu'an in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guozhen, courtesy name Yanfu, came from Gu'an in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖藹，祖蟾，父絢，代襲儒素。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ai, grandfather Chan, and father Xuan for generations inherited the tradition of scholarly plain living.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears Ai, Chan, and Xuan for generations upheld a scholar's plain way of life.

sentences.zh: 國珍少值燕薊亂離，因落發被緇，客於河西延州，高萬興兄弟皆好文，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Guozhen in youth encountered the turmoil and separation of Yan and Ji; he therefore shaved his head and donned the black robe, sojourned at Yan Prefecture in Hexi, and because the brothers Gao Wanxing all loved literature, they recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived through the chaos of Yan and Ji, took Buddhist orders, and sojourned at Yan Prefecture in Hexi, where the Gao Wanxing brothers, lovers of letters, took him onto their staff.

sentences.zh: 國珍常以文章自許，求貢禮闈，且掌書奏，期年，入為左拾遺，累遷至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Guozhen often prided himself on his literary compositions, sought to present tribute at the civil examination hall, and also managed documents and memorials; within a year he entered court as Left Reminder and through successive promotions rose to a director under the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his writing, he sought the civil examinations, handled documents and memorials, and within a year entered court as Left Reminder, rising eventually to a secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 每與人交，傾財無吝。

translations.literal: Whenever he associated with others he poured out his wealth without stint.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he spent freely without stint.

sentences.zh: 性頗剛僻，經藝史學，非其所長，好自矜衒，多上章疏，文字差誤，數數有之，為縉紳所誚。

translations.literal: His nature was rather stubborn and eccentric; classical learning and historical studies were not his strengths; he loved to boast and display himself, submitted many memorials, and textual errors occurred again and again, for which he was ridiculed by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn and eccentric, he lacked real mastery of the classics or history, loved self-display, filed frequent memorials riddled with errors, and was mocked by the gentry.

sentences.zh: 高祖在藩時，嘗通私謁，以兄事之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still in his princely domain he once paid him private visits and treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince Gaozu visited him privately and treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及即位，國珍自比於嚴陵，上表敘舊，由是自吏部郎中拜左諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yan Ling and submitted a memorial recounting their old ties; thereby, from Director in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor and Censor-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Guozhen likened himself to Yan Guang, memorialized on their old friendship, and rose from personnel director to Left Remonstrance Counselor and censor-in-attendance.

translations.literal: [Annotation:]
translations.idiomatic: [Annotation:]

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史·張彥澤傳》：國珍與御史中丞王易簡率三院御史詣閣門，連疏論張彥澤，不報。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Ouyang History, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen together with Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led censors of the three bureaus to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat and submitted successive memorials criticizing Zhang Yanze, without response.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang History, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the three bureaus' censors to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat with successive memorials against Zhang Yanze, but received no reply.")〉

sentences.zh: 又求為御史中丞，時宰政不復為請，國珍銜之。

translations.literal: He again requested appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers at the time no longer memorialized on his behalf, and Guozhen harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He sought the post of censor-in-chief again, but the chief ministers would not press his case, and he bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 李崧之母薨，遣諸弟護喪歸葬深州，崧既起復，乃出北郊路隅設奠，公卿大夫皆送喪而出，國珍固爭不行，眾鹹推其讜直。

translations.literal: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the coffin home for burial in Shen Prefecture; Song had already returned to office from mourning, yet went out to the roadside at the northern suburb to set out offerings; dukes, ministers, and grandees all went out to escort the funeral, but Guozhen firmly argued and would not go; the multitude all praised his forthright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Song's mother died he sent his brothers to bury her in Shen Prefecture; though Song had resumed office, he set out offerings at a roadside shrine north of the city and the whole court turned out for the funeral procession—Guozhen alone refused to go, and all admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 高祖晏駕，朝廷以宰臣馮道為山陵使，及靈盾既發，國珍上疏言：「馮道既為山陵使，不得復入都城，請除外佐，以桑維翰入輔。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, the court appointed chief minister Feng Dao as commissioner for the imperial tomb; after the spirit shield had set out, Guozhen submitted a memorial saying: "Since Feng Dao is commissioner for the imperial tomb, he must not again enter the capital city; I request that he be excluded as an assistant and that Sang Weihan enter to assist governance."
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death Feng Dao was made tomb commissioner; once the funeral procession had departed Guozhen memorialized: "Feng Dao, as tomb commissioner, must not return to the capital—replace him with Sang Weihan as chief assistant."

sentences.zh: 李崧請罷相位，俾持喪制。

translations.literal: Li Song should be asked to relinquish the chief minister's post and be allowed to observe mourning regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song should leave the chief ministership to observe proper mourning.

sentences.zh: 」少帝覽奏，以所言侵越，出為陜州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: " The Young Emperor read the memorial and, because the words were presumptuous and overstepping, sent him out as acting military adjutant of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor, deeming the memorial presumptuous, banished him to Shaan Prefecture as acting military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 至任悒怏，遘疾而卒。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he was depressed and discontented, encountered illness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he languished in discontent, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 張仁願，字善政，開封陳留人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Renyuan, courtesy name Shanzheng, was a native of Chenliu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renyuan, courtesy name Shanzheng, came from Chenliu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖晸，唐右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing was General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing had been General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 父存敬，梁河中節度觀察留後，累贈中書令，《梁書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Cunjing was military governor's observation regent at Hezhong under Liang, and through successive posthumous promotions was raised to Palace Secretariat Director; the Liang History contains his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunjing had been observation regent at Hezhong under the Liang and was posthumously ennobled to Palace Secretariat Director; the Liang History records his life.

sentences.zh: 仁願梁貞明初，以勛臣之子起家為衛尉寺主簿，改著作佐郎、左贊善大夫，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming under Liang, as the son of a meritorious official Renyuan began his career as chief clerk of the Imperial Guard Office, was changed to Assistant in the Bureau of Writings and Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and was granted the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang's Zhenming era he entered office as chief clerk of the Imperial Guard Office as a meritorious official's son, became assistant in the Bureau of Writings and Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and received the crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 唐同光初，遷大理正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang under Tang he was transferred to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang's Tongguang era he became director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，自將作少監轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was transferred from Vice Director of the Directorate of Works to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 1 he moved from vice director of works to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷昭武、歸德兩鎮節度判官。

translations.literal: During Changxing he served successively as judge of the Zhaowu and Guide military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he served as judge on the Zhaowu and Guide military commissions.

sentences.zh: 四年，復入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again entered court as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，除殿中監。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Palace Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he became Director of the Palace Receptions.

sentences.zh: 天福五年，拜大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 he was appointed minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 仁願性溫雅，明法書，累居詳刑之地，議讞疑獄，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Renyuan's nature was mild and refined; he was skilled in penal law and calligraphy; he repeatedly held posts in detailed punishment, deliberated doubtful cases, and was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and refined, skilled in law and calligraphy, he long held judicial posts, deliberated difficult cases, and was reckoned thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 兄仁穎，梁朝仕至諸衛將軍，中年以風恙廢於家凡十餘年，仁願事之，出告反面，如嚴父焉，士大夫推為孝友。

translations.literal: His elder brother Renying under Liang rose in office to general of the guards; in mid-life, afflicted with wind ailment, he was disabled at home for more than ten years; Renyuan served him, reporting when going out and returning when coming in, as to a strict father, and scholar-officials praised him for filial brotherly conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Renying had risen to general of the guards under the Liang but spent his last decade bedridden with rheumatism; Renyuan attended him with the punctilio due a father, and the gentry praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 仁穎善理家，勤而且約，婦女衣不曳地，什物多歷年所，如新市焉。

translations.literal: Renying was skilled at managing the household, diligent and moreover frugal; women's garments did not trail on the ground, and many household goods after years of use were still like new from the market.
translations.idiomatic: Renying ran the household with tireless thrift—women's hems never swept the floor, and goods years old looked newly bought.

sentences.zh: 仁願開運元年再為大理卿，時隰州刺史王澈犯贓，朝廷以澈功臣之後，欲宥之，仁願累執奏不移，竟遣伏法，議者賞之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun Renyuan again became Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; at that time Wang Che, Prefect of Xi Prefecture, committed corruption; the court, because Che was descended from a meritorious official, wished to pardon him, but Renyuan repeatedly memorialized and would not yield, and in the end Che was sent to execution by law; commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 1 he again became minister of the Court of Judicial Review; when Xi prefect Wang Che was convicted of corruption the court wished to spare him as a meritorious family's son, but Renyuan's repeated memorials held firm until Che was executed—an act commentators applauded.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，以疾卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he died of illness, at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in Kaiyun 2, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 趙熙，字績巨，唐宰相齊國公光逢之猶子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Jiju, was a nephew of Tang chief minister Duke of Qi Guo Guangfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Jiju, was a nephew of the Tang chief minister Duke of Qi, Zhao Guangfeng.

sentences.zh: 起家授秘書省校書郎，唐天成中，累遷至起居郎。

translations.literal: He began his career with appointment as collator in the Secretariat; during Tiancheng under Tang he was successively promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a secretariat collator and during Tang's Tiancheng era rose to diarist.

sentences.zh: 數上章言事，以稱旨尋除南省正郎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs; because his words pleased the intent of the throne he was soon appointed a regular director in the southern ministries.
translations.idiomatic: His frequent memorials pleased the throne and soon won him a regular director's post in the southern ministries.

sentences.zh: 天福中，承詔與張昭遠等修《唐史》，竟集其功。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he received orders together with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others to compile the Tang History, and in the end gathered its achievement to completion.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he was ordered with Zhang Zhaoyuan and others to compile the Tang History and brought the project to completion.

sentences.zh: 開運中，自兵部郎中授右諫議大夫，賞筆削之功也。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun he was promoted from Director in the Ministry of War to Right Remonstrance Counselor, in reward for his brush-and-knife editorial work.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun he rose from war ministry director to Right Remonstrance Counselor in reward for his editorial labors on the history.

sentences.zh: 及契丹犯闕，偽旨遣使於晉州率配豪民錢幣，以實行橐。

translations.literal: When the Khitans violated the capital, by forged edict an envoy was sent to Jin Prefecture to levy assessments on wealthy households for money and goods to fill the traveling bags.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans seized the capital a forged edict sent him to Jin Prefecture to levy money from wealthy households to fill the invaders' baggage.

sentences.zh: 始受命之日，條制甚嚴，熙出衣冠族，性素輕急，既畏契丹峻法，乃窮理搜索，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: From the day he first received the commission the regulations were very strict; Xi came from the cap-and-gown clans and his nature had always been light and hasty; now fearing the Khitans' severe laws, he pursued investigations to the utmost in searching, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From his first day in office the rules were harsh; Xi, born to the gentry and by nature impulsive, feared the Khitans' severity and searched households relentlessly until the people were in misery.

sentences.zh: 及晉之三軍殺副使駱從朗，

translations.literal: When the three armies of Jin killed Vice Commissioner Luo Conglang,
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's three armies killed vice commissioner Luo Conglang,

translations.literal: [Annotation:]
translations.idiomatic: [Annotation:]

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：契丹以節度副使駱從朗知晉州事，大將藥可儔殺從朗。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: The Khitans appointed Vice Commissioner Luo Conglang to administer Jin Prefecture affairs; the great general Yao Kechou killed Conglang.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: The Khitans put vice commissioner Luo Conglang in charge of Jin Prefecture; the general Yao Kechou killed him.")〉

sentences.zh: 百姓相率持仗害熙於館舍，識者傷之。

translations.literal: the common people in succession took up weapons and killed Xi at the guest lodge; those who knew him grieved.
translations.idiomatic: the populace rose with weapons and killed Xi at his lodging; those who knew him mourned.

sentences.zh: 李遐，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Li Xia was a native of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xia came from Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為儒，有節操。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar and possessed moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied the classics and held fast to principle.

sentences.zh: 歷數鎮從事，及升朝，累遷尚書庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as staff officer in several commands; when he rose to court he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Director in the Department of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served on several military staffs and, after entering court, rose to outer director in the Ministry of Works' Department of Storehouses.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以皇子重乂保釐洛邑，知遐強幹有守，除為西京留守判官，使之佐理，復重其廉勤，兼委監西京左藏庫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, because the imperial prince Chongyi was securing and rectifying Luoyang, knowing that Xia was strong, capable, and steadfast, he appointed him judge of the western capital regent, to assist in governance; he again valued his incorrupt diligence and concurrently entrusted him to supervise the western capital's left treasury storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozu's accession Prince Chongyi was securing Luoyang; knowing Xia's strength and integrity, Gaozu made him judge to the western capital regent and later also put him in charge of the western capital's left treasury.

sentences.zh: 會張從賓作亂，使人輦取繒帛以賞群逆，遐曰：「不奉詔書，安敢承命！

translations.literal: When Zhang Congbin rebelled, he sent men to cart away silks and fabrics to reward the band of rebels; Xia said: "Without receiving an imperial edict, how dare I accept the command!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Congbin rebelled his men came to cart off silk from the treasury to reward the rebels; Xia said: "Without an imperial edict I dare not obey!"

sentences.zh: 」遂為其下所害。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon killed by their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates then killed him.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘆惜，賻贈加等，仍贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed in regret, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and also posthumously granted him Right Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed in grief, raised his funeral gifts one grade, and posthumously made him Right Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 其母田氏，封京兆郡太君，仍給遐所食月俸，終母餘年。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Tian, was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and Xia's monthly salary was still paid until his mother's remaining years were ended.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Tian was enfeoffed Grand Lady of Jingzhao Commandery, and his salary continued to be paid for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 其子俟服闋與官。

translations.literal: His son was to receive office when mourning was completed.
translations.idiomatic: His son was promised office once mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 後又遣兗州節度使李從溫就其舊業，賜牲幣綿帛等物，以旌其忠也。

translations.literal: Later Yan military commissioner Li Congwen was also sent to his former post, and sacrificial victims, silks, cottons, and other goods were granted to honor his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan commissioner Li Congwen was sent to his former post with sacrificial goods, silk, and cotton to honor his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 尹玉羽，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yin Yuyu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuyu came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐天福中，隨計京師，甚有文稱。

translations.literal: During Tianfu under Tang he followed the examination procession to the capital and enjoyed a great literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tianfu era he went to the capital for the examinations and earned a strong literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 會有苴杖之喪，累歲羸疾，冬不釋菅屨，期不變倚廬。

translations.literal: He happened to suffer the mourning with hemp staff; for successive years he was frail and ill, in winter never laying aside straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period never changing his lean-to by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When a parent died he mourned for years in frail health, wore straw sandals even in winter, and never left the mourning hut by the tomb.

sentences.zh: 制闋，隱居杜門，無仕宦之意。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he lived in seclusion behind closed doors and had no intention of entering official service.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he shut his doors to the world and had no wish for office.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，劉鄩辟為保大軍節度判官，歷雍、汴、滑、兗從事。

translations.literal: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Yun recruited him as judge of the Baoda Army military commission; he served successively as staff officer in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang's Zhenming era Liu Yun made him judge on the Baoda Army commission, and he later served on staffs in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.

translations.literal: [Annotation:]
translations.idiomatic: [Annotation:]

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕。

translations.literal: (Note: There is a lacuna below.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The text below is defective.

sentences.zh: 考宋黎持《移石經紀》：石經舊在務本坊，自天祐中韓建築新城，而石經委棄於野。

translations.literal: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: the stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built a new city, and the stone classics were cast away in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics notes that the classics had stood in Wuben Ward until Han Jian built a new city in the Tianyou era and left them abandoned in the open country.

sentences.zh: 至朱梁時，劉鄩守長安，從幕吏尹玉羽之請，輦入城中，置於此地，即唐尚書省之西隅也。）〉

translations.literal: By the time of the Zhu Liang, Liu Yun guarded Chang'an; following the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, they were carted into the city and placed at this spot, namely the western corner of the Tang Secretariat.")〉
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Liang, when Liu Yun held Chang'an, he carted them into the city at staff officer Yin Yuyu's request and set them at the western corner of the Tang Secretariat.")〉

sentences.zh: 唐清泰中，為光祿少卿，退歸秦中，以林泉詩酒自樂，自號自然先生。

translations.literal: During Qingtai under Tang he was Vice Director of the Imperial Household; he retired to Qinzhong and took pleasure in forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Natural.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Qingtai era he was vice director of the imperial household, then retired to the Qin region, enjoying forests, streams, poetry, and wine under the name Master Natural.

sentences.zh: 宰臣張延朗手書而召，高臥不從，謂人曰：「庶孽代宗，不可仕也。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him with a letter in his own hand, but he lay high and would not comply, saying to others: "A bastard has replaced the legitimate line—one cannot serve."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by personal letter, but he refused to rise, saying: "A bastard sits on the throne—I will not serve."

sentences.zh: 」及高祖入洛，即受詔而來，以所著《自然經》五卷貢之，且告其老。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu entered Luoyang he at once received the edict and came, presented as tribute his five-juan Classic of the Natural in composition, and also reported his old age.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he obeyed the summons, presented his five-juan Classic of the Natural, and pleaded old age.

sentences.zh: 即日璽書褒美，頒其器幣，授少府監致仕，月給俸錢及冬春二時服。

translations.literal: That very day an imperial letter in the seal script praised him, bestowed vessels and silks, appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Workshops with retirement, and granted monthly salary money and garments for the two seasons of winter and spring.
translations.idiomatic: That day an imperial letter praised him, granted gifts of vessels and silk, named him vice director of palace workshops with retirement pay, and awarded monthly salary plus winter and spring garments.

sentences.zh: 天福中，卒，有《武庫集》五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he died; his fifty-juan Armory Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Tianfu; his fifty-juan Armory Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲叟，本名遨，雲叟其字也，以唐明宗廟諱，故世傳其字焉，本南燕人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunsou, original name Ao, Yunsou being his courtesy name; because of the taboo on Emperor Mingzong's temple name under Tang, the world therefore transmitted his courtesy name; he was originally a native of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunsou, born Ao, took Yunsou as his courtesy name; because of the taboo on Mingzong's temple name posterity knew him by that courtesy name; he came from Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，耿介不屈。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was upright and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied hard and was upright and unbending.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗朝，嘗應進士舉，不第，因欲攜妻子隱於林壑，其妻非之，不肯行，雲叟乃薄遊諸郡，獲數百緡以贍其家，辭訣而去。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once entered the jinshi examination and did not pass; he therefore wished to take wife and children to hide in forests and ravines; his wife disapproved and would not go; Yunsou then traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhaozong he failed the jinshi examination and wished to take his family into the mountains; his wife refused, so he traveled the provinces, earned several hundred strings of cash for their support, bade farewell, and left.

sentences.zh: 尋入少室山，著《擬峰詩》三十六章，以導其趣，人多傳之。

translations.literal: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi, composed thirty-six chapters of Imitating Peak Poetry to guide his inclination, and many people transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered Mount Shaoshi, wrote thirty-six chapters of Imitating Peak Poetry to express his temperament, and many copied them.

sentences.zh: 後妻以書達意，勸其還家，雲叟未嘗一覽，悉投於火，其絕累如此。

translations.literal: Later his wife sent a letter conveying her thoughts and urging him to return home; Yunsou never once looked at it and cast it all into the fire—such was his severing of entanglements.
translations.idiomatic: Later his wife wrote urging him home; he never opened the letter and burned it—so thoroughly had he cut worldly ties.

sentences.zh: 俄聞西嶽有五鬛松，淪脂千年，能去三屍，因居於華陰。

translations.literal: Before long he heard that on the Western Peak there was a five-tufted pine whose oozing resin after a thousand years could expel the three corpses, and therefore he dwelt at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of a five-tufted pine on the Western Peak whose millennial resin could expel the three corpses, he settled at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 與李道殷、羅隱之友善，時人目為「三高士」。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Li Daoyin and Luo Yin, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Li Daoyin and Luo Yin, whom contemporaries called the Three High Recluses.

sentences.zh: 道殷有釣魚之術，鉤而不餌，又能化易金石，無所不至，雲叟恒目睹其事，信而不求。

translations.literal: Daoyin had the art of fishing with a hook but no bait, and could also transform and change metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do; Yunsou constantly witnessed these affairs, believed yet did not seek them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyin could fish with a bare hook and transmute metal and stone at will; Yunsou often saw it, believed, yet never sought the art for himself.

sentences.zh: 雲叟與梁室權臣李振善，振欲祿之，拒而不諾，及振南遷，雲叟千里徒步以省之，識者高焉。

translations.literal: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, powerful minister of the Liang house; Zhen wished to grant him salary and office, but he refused and would not consent; when Zhen moved south, Yunsou walked a thousand li on foot to visit him, and those who knew him held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Later Liang power minister Li Zhen, who offered him office; Yunsou refused. When Zhen was sent south, Yunsou walked a thousand li on foot to visit him—a gesture men of discernment greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 後妻兒繼謝，每聞兇服，一哭而止。

translations.literal: Later his wife and children sent successive letters of thanks; whenever he heard of mourning garments he wept once and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children later sent thanks; whenever news of mourning reached him he wept once and no more.

sentences.zh: 時惟青衿二童子、一琴、一鶴，從其遊處。

translations.literal: At that time only two youths in blue collars, one zither, and one crane accompanied him wherever he wandered.
translations.idiomatic: Only two blue-clad boys, a zither, and a crane accompanied him on his wanderings.

sentences.zh: 好棋塞之戲，遇同侶則以晝繼夜，雖寒風大雪，臨檐對局，手足皸裂，亦無倦焉。

translations.literal: He loved the games of chess and frontier checkers; when he met companions he continued day into night; even in cold wind and heavy snow, facing each other under the eaves over the board, with hands and feet chapped and cracked, he still knew no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He loved chess and frontier checkers and, with a companion, would play day into night; even in driving snow under the eaves, hands and feet cracked with cold, he never tired.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，召拜左拾遺，不起。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng under Tang he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tiancheng era he was summoned as Left Reminder but declined.

sentences.zh: 與羅隱之朝夕遊處，隱之以藥術取利，雲叟以山田自給，俱好酒能詩，善長嘯。

translations.literal: He spent mornings and evenings in company with Luo Yin; Yin profited by medical arts, while Yunsou supported himself by mountain fields; both loved wine and could compose poetry, and were skilled at long whistling.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days with Luo Yin, who lived by medicine while Yunsou farmed the hills; both loved wine and poetry and were masters of the long whistle.

sentences.zh: 有大瓠，雲可辟寒暑，置酒於其中，經時味不壞，日攜就花木水石之間，一酌一詠。

translations.literal: He had a great gourd said to ward off cold and heat; he placed wine in it and after a long time the flavor did not spoil; daily he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and stones, taking one sip and one recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He owned a great gourd said to temper heat and cold; wine kept in it never spoiled, and each day he carried it among flowers and streams for a drink and a poem.

sentences.zh: 嘗因酒酣聯句，鄭曰：「一壺天上有名物，兩個世間無事人。

translations.literal: Once, when wine had warmed them, they composed linked verses; Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from Heaven above; two men—carefree people in the mortal world."
translations.idiomatic: Once, deep in wine, they composed linked verses; Zheng said: "One jar—a thing of fame from heaven; two men—without a care in the world."

sentences.zh: 」羅曰：「醉卻隱之、雲叟外，不知何處是天真。

translations.literal: " Luo said: "Drunk beyond Yin and Yunsou, one no longer knows where true innocence lies."
translations.idiomatic: Luo replied: "Once drunk, beyond Yin and Yunsou, who knows where true innocence is?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖即位，聞其名，遣使賫書致禮，征為右諫議大夫，雲叟稱疾不起，上表陳謝。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu took the throne he heard of his name, sent an envoy bearing a letter to present ritual gifts, and summoned him as Right Remonstrance Counselor; Yunsou pleaded illness and would not rise, submitting a memorial to decline with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he sent gifts and summoned Yunsou as Right Remonstrance Counselor; Yunsou pleaded illness and memorialized his thanks for declining.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，賜近臣傳觀，尋賜號逍遙先生，以諫議大夫致仕，月給俸祿。

translations.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, granting the inner ministers to pass it around for viewing; soon he bestowed the title Master Free Wanderer, allowed retirement as Remonstrance Counselor, and granted monthly salary.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu admired the memorial and had it shown to his inner ministers, then granted him the title Master Free Wanderer, retirement as remonstrance counselor, and a monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 雲叟好酒，嘗為《詠酒詩》千二百言，海內好名者書於縑緗，以為贈貺。

translations.literal: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred words; those within the seas who loved fame copied it on silk and gave it as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: A lover of wine, he once wrote a twelve-hundred-word Ode to Wine that admirers across the realm copied onto silk as gifts.

sentences.zh: 復有越千里之外，使畫工潛寫其形容列為屏障者焉。

translations.literal: There were also those beyond a thousand li who sent painters secretly to sketch his likeness and array it as screen panels.
translations.idiomatic: Some from more than a thousand li away even sent painters to sketch him secretly for screen panels.

sentences.zh: 其為時望所重也如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held by the expectations of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which his contemporaries held him.

sentences.zh: 天福末，以壽終，時年七十四。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he ended his life by longevity, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age late in Tianfu, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in twenty juan circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古攀龍鱗，附鳳翼，坐達於雲衢者，豈獨豐沛之士哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: From antiquity those who climbed dragon scales and attached themselves to phoenix wings, reaching the cloud highways while seated—were they only men of Feng and Pei!
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Since antiquity, those who rose by clinging to dragon scales and phoenix wings to reach the highways of power—were they only the men of Feng and Pei!

sentences.zh: 茍懷才抱器，適會興王，亦可以取貴於一時，如盧質而下數君子是也。

translations.literal: If one harbors talent and embraces ability, and happens to meet a rising sovereign, one may also win honor for a time—such are the several gentlemen from Lu Zhi downward.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds talent and meets a rising sovereign, one may still win honor for a season—such were Lu Zhi and the gentlemen below him.

sentences.zh: 至如國珍之讜直，仁願之友悌，趙、李二子沒於王事，皆無忝於士林矣。

translations.literal: As for Guozhen's forthright integrity, Renyuan's brotherly filial affection, and the two gentlemen Zhao and Li who perished in royal service—all were without shame to the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's integrity, Renyuan's brotherly devotion, and Zhao and Li, who died in the state's service—all did honor to the scholar class.

sentences.zh: 唯玉羽之貞退，雲叟之肥遁，足可以柅奔競之風，激高尚之節也。

translations.literal: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were sufficient to check the wind of frantic competition and stir the integrity of lofty principle.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuyu's steadfast retirement and Yunsou's full withdrawal were enough to bridle the rush for rank and rouse a nobler standard of conduct.
